paragraphs.source_en: Mr. Tofu drained the tea, now gone cold, in one determined gulp, and said with great solemnity, “The reason I have called today is that there is a small matter I should like to ask of you.” “Ah, what matter might that be?” My master, too, assumed an equally serious air. “As you probably know, I am very fond of literature and the fine arts...” said Mr. Tofu. “Excellent.” My master encouraged him. “Since the other day, a number of us who share the same interests have gathered together and formed a reading society. We meet once a month, intending to continue our studies in this direction; indeed, our first meeting was already held at the end of last year.” “Allow me to ask: when you say a reading society, it sounds as if you recite poems, essays, and the like with some sort of rhythm. How exactly do you conduct it?” “No, at first we read works by writers of old, and then, little by little, we mean to take up works by our own members.” “By works of the ancients, do you mean something like Bai Letian’s ‘Song of the Pipa’?” “No.” “Something like Buson’s ‘Spring Wind on the Kema Embankment’?” “No.” “Then what did you perform?” “The other day we did one of Chikamatsu’s lovers’ suicide plays.” “Chikamatsu? You mean Chikamatsu, the writer of joruri puppet plays?” There are not two Chikamatsus in the world. Once one says Chikamatsu, it is of course Chikamatsu the playwright. For my master to ask again was, I thought, profoundly foolish. But my master had not the least idea what I was thinking, and continued kindly stroking my head. In this world there are many people who mistake a squint for an amorous glance, so my master’s little misunderstanding was hardly surprising; I therefore sat there composedly and let him stroke me. “Yes,” Mr. Tofu replied, stealing a glance at my master’s expression. “Then do you read it alone, or do you divide up the roles?” “We assigned roles to one another and tried it once in dialogue form. Our aim is, as far as possible, to sympathize with the characters in the work, to bring out their personalities fully, and to add gestures and movements as well. In the dialogue, the chief thing is to reproduce people of that period; whether a young lady or an apprentice boy, each role is to be made vividly present.” “In that case, is what you do not much the same as acting?” The visitor replied, “Exactly. It merely lacks costumes and scenery.” My master asked again, “Pardon my frankness, but does it go well?” The visitor said, “Well, for a first attempt I think it may be called a success.” My master asked, “You said the piece you did last time was a lovers’ suicide play. Which scene was it?” The visitor said, “It was the scene where the boatman ferries a customer to Yoshiwara.” “That is rather a formidable scene.” Being a teacher, my master showed a degree of misgiving on that point. The smoke of the Hinode cigarette he blew from his nostrils skimmed past his ear and drifted around the side of his face.

paragraphs.source_zh: 东风君将放冷了的茶狠狠地一饮而尽，郑重其事地说道：“今天来拜访，是有点事情想托您。”“啊，是什么事情？”主人也同样一本正经起来。“您大概知道，我很喜欢文学、美术……”东风君说。“好极了。”主人鼓励说。“从前些日子起，我们一些同好之士聚在一起，组织了一个朗读会，每月聚会一次，今后想继续这方面的研究，第一次会合，已在去年底举行过了。”“请允许我问一下，所谓朗读会，听起来大概是带上某种节奏来朗诵诗歌、文章之类的吧，你们究竟是怎么个搞法？”“哪里，最初先朗读一些古人的作品，然后，我们打算逐渐搞同人的作品。”“所谓古人的作品，是指白乐天的《琵琶行》之类的作品吗？”“不是。”“是芜村的《春风马堤曲》那类的东西吗？”“不是。”“那你们搞了些什么呢？”“前一阵搞了近松的‘情死剧’。”“近松？就是那个写净琉璃脚本的近松吗？”天下哪有两个近松，既然说是近松，当然是剧作家近松无疑。主人却一问再问，真是蠢得很。可是，主人丝毫不知道我的这种想法，还在很亲切地抚摸着我的头。在这个世上，有不少人误把斜视眼当作是送秋波，主人的这点阴差阳错也毫不足怪，所以我也就心安理得地任凭他抚摸着。“是的，”东风君答了一句，偷看了一下主人的脸色。“那么，你们是由一个人朗读，还是分担角色去搞呢？”“我们各自分配一个角色，已经在一起搞过一次了。我们的宗旨是尽可能对作品中的人物寄予同情，充分表现其人物的性格，而且还要加进一些手势或动作。在对白方面主要是再现出那个时代的人，不管是小姐，还是小徒弟，都要把每个角色活灵活现地表现出来。”“那么说，你们搞的不是和演戏差不多吗？”客人回答：“可不是嘛，只是不穿戏装，没有布景罢了。”主人又问道：“恕我冒昧问一下，你们搞的还成功吗？”客人说：“是啊，我想作为第一次来说应该算是成功的吧。”主人问道：“你说上次搞的是情死剧，那是什么剧目呢？”客人说：“是船老大把嫖客摆渡到吉原去的那一场。”“那可是一场相当够呛的戏哩。”主人不愧是个教师，对此表示出几分疑义。从他鼻孔喷出的“日出牌”香烟的烟雾，掠过他的耳旁，由脸后横飘过去。

paragraphs.source_en: “No, there was really nothing so formidable about it. The characters on stage were only the customer, the boatman, the courtesan, the waitress, the brothel matron, and the kenban.” It seemed that Mr. Tofu was quite unconcerned about such matters. When my master heard the word “courtesan,” he could not help frowning slightly. But as for the terms “waitress,” “brothel matron,” and “kenban,” he appeared to lack precise knowledge, and so first raised a question: “Does ‘waitress’ mean a maidservant in a brothel?” “I have not yet studied it thoroughly. However, I think a ‘waitress’ is a maid at a teahouse. As for the brothel matron, she is probably something like an assistant manager in the women’s quarters.” This Mr. Tofu had just declared that he would use assumed voices to bring the characters’ personalities to life, yet it seemed he did not understand the nature of such characters as the brothel matron and the waitress. My master went on, “Oh, I see. The waitress belongs to the teahouse, and the brothel matron lives in the house of prostitution, is that it? Then is this ‘kenban’ a person, or does it refer to some particular place? If it is a person, is it a man or a woman?” The visitor said, “I think the kenban is probably a man.” My master said, “And what is he in charge of?” “Well, I have not carried my research that far yet. I shall look into it carefully later.”
